The test instantiates `cfnlint.template.transforms._language_extensions._Transform` and runs `transform(cfn)` over `_TEMPLATE`. The static factory `_ForEachValue.create(obj)` (lines 234-250 of `_language_extensions.py`) dispatches polymorphically: scalar -> `_ForEachValue`; dict whose single key is `Ref` -> `_ForEachValueRef`; `Fn::FindInMap` -> `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap`; `Fn::If` -> `_ForEachValueFnIf`; otherwise raise. Capture the EXACT concrete class type RETURNED BY EVERY CALL TO `_ForEachValue.create` IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER OF RETURN EVENT during this test execution. Return the answer under the field `dispatch_sequence` -- a list of class name strings (e.g. `"_ForEachValue"`, `"_ForEachValueRef"`). Subtle rules to simulate: (1) Subclass constructors themselves call `create` internally: `_ForEachValueRef.__init__` calls `create(obj)` for the inner string; `_ForEachValueFnIf.__init__` calls `create(obj[0])` for the condition name; `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap.__init__` calls `create(obj[0])`, `create(obj[1])`, `create(obj[2])` left-to-right for its list-triple. The INNER calls RETURN BEFORE the OUTER call, so the chronology is depth-first post-order at each subclass construction. (2) `_ForEach.__init__` (constructed once per outer ForEach key during template parsing) does `create(value[0])` (loop var name) and `create(item)` for each list item in the collection. (3) The TOP-LEVEL `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap` instantiated by `_walk`'s Fn::FindInMap branch is built by DIRECT constructor call -- NOT routed through `create` -- so it does NOT appear in the dispatch sequence. Only NESTED FindInMaps (one FindInMap as the argument of another) appear, because the inner one is routed through `create`. (4) `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap.value(...)` has a fallback path starting at line 366: when `t_map[1].value(...)` raises `_ResolveError` (e.g. for an `Fn::If` arg), the fallback iterates the resolved mapping and calls `_ForEachValue.create(k)` for EVERY key whose value-dict contains `t_map[2].value()`. There is NO break, so all matching keys yield a create event and the LAST one wins as the new `t_map[1]`. (5) Each iteration of the outer Fn::ForEach walks the body afresh, so the per-iteration creates duplicate across iterations in iteration order. (6) Body Properties dict iterates in INSERTION order: `Mapped` -> `Mapped2` -> `Mapped3`.
